note: Second unseen set: 100 messages in a mixed, everyday spread (county offices, consultants, homeowners, firm staff notes, and messages with nothing to file), written by an AI author who read the 72 examples, the first unseen set and the claim vocabulary, and did not read the readers' instructions, code or recorded output. FINAL KEY: two labellers labelled the set blind (labels_A.json, labels_B.json); an adjudicator who did not read the readers' instructions, code or output, nor the author's key, decided every statement only one of them gave, from the message text, the packet and the written conventions (adjudication.md). key_status.json marks each statement as "both" or "adjudicated". "expect_no_effect" is true where the list is empty or holds only acknowledgement or internal_note, and null elsewhere because the engine was not run on the labels. "trap" is left null. The labels use the newest claim types, so score with --labels-current. Each message is read on its own at the end of the examples; the messages do not form one consistent timeline.
